BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. -L S. 26L FEB 1 3 2025 G. VOLTER ERIC S. ESPIRITU President Purok 7 Proper Acacia Neighborhood Association Inc. Alabang, Muntinlupa City Dear Mr. Espiritu: This has reference to your letter dated 14 July 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion regarding the following matters: 1. Matuturing po bang election offense ang City Ordinance No. 2022-263 sa kadahilanang naipasa po ito ilang araw bagong magsimula ang panglokal ng kampanya nong 2022? 2. Maari po bang hindi sinundin ng kasalukuyang administrasyon ng Pamahalaang Lokal ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa ang City Ordinance No. 2017-098 0 and Revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan (2016-026) na nagtatalaga sa aming lugar bilang Social Housing Site? 3. Kung ang City Ordinance No. 2017-098 0 ang Revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan (2016-2026) ay dapat sundin ng Pamahalaang Lokal ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa at kung ito ay lalabagin, may karampatan bang parusa and maaring ipataw sa Pamahalaang Lokal ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa? Per the representation, the Local Government of Muntinlupa City is preparing to evict you and other families since the property on which your house was built was purchased by the LGU. You claimed that the main reason for your probable eviction was Muntinlupa City Ordinance No. 2017-98, also known as the Revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP) 2016-2026, which was passed on March 23, 2022, a few months before previous Mayor Jaime Fresnedi's term ended. You then claimed that the land was officially transferred on June 22, 2022, under the name Muntinlupa City. You mentioned that Muntinlupa City issued notices to vacate and gave you 30 days to vacate the subject property, but you ignored them and claimed that you should not be evicted because you were born and raised on the land. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

You then mentioned that the Muntinlupa LGU has provided a relocation because the eviction will purportedly affect 80 people. In this regard, you are questioning the legitimacy of Muntinlupa City Ordinance No. 2017-98, because it requires the construction of a Socialized Housing Site on the subject land. However, you claimed that the Muntinlupa Local Government will build a Mega Health Centre on the subject site. Thus, the request for legal opinion. As to the first query, it is respectfully advised that the matter is best addressed to the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), as it squarely falls within its jurisdiction and authority as the constitutional body mandated to oversee and regulate electoral matters. Regarding the second query, the response is in the negative. It is a fundamental principle that all laws must be strictly observed, as adherence to the rule of law is a cornerstone of governance in the Philippines. This principle ensures that all individuals, institutions, and government entities are held accountable to laws that are duly enacted, equally applied, and consistent with the fundamental rights enshrined in the Constitution. Compliance with the law is essential to maintain order, promote justice, and uphold the integrity of governmental processes. Here, the City Ordinance No. 2017-098 is lawfully enacted and thus, must be enforced and followed. Unless invalidity or unreasonableness is ostensibly apparent, one seeking a judicial declaration of the invalidity of an ordinance is duty-bound to adduce evidence that is convincingly indicative of its infirmities or defects.l Until after the judiciary, in appropriate case, declare its invalidity, it is entitled to obedience and respect.2 On the third query, we respond in the affirmative. Officials of a Local Government Unit (LGU) may be held liable for violations of an ordinance. Pursuant to the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160), LGUs and their officials are mandated to comply with and enforce ordinances enacted in the exercise of local legislative powers. Once an ordinance is duly enacted, it becomes the duty of the LGU to ensure its implementation and enforcement. With regard to the City's non-enforcement of the Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP), it bears emphasis that DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2024-084, dated June 20, 2024, explicitly provides that the failure of LGUs to comply with the requirements for the preparation, updating, or enforcement of CLUPs and Zoning Ordinances may give rise to administrative liability. This provision underscores the accountability of LGU officials in ensuring adherence to land use and zoning policies, which are essential for the orderly development and management of their respective jurisdictions. In light of the foregoing, LGU officials are enjoined to strictly comply with the provisions of enacted ordinances, including the enforcement of the CLUP, to avoid potential administrative sanctions and to uphold the principles of good governance. 1 DILG Opinion No. 44, series of 2024, April 16, 2024 2 Hagedorn, et al., V. COA, G.R. No. 260458, June 04, 2024 Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: OMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/RPB/LLLS-LRALLD/lasm/kbm Page 3 of 3
